text: Levan Makhashvili - Both the European Parliament's documents and the European Parliament itself have, unfortunately, lost their value—the only thing left is a sporting interest: to see whether they will develop a document worse than the previous one or if we will have something new. (05.05.2026, 14:29)

"This document, along with its amendments which have made the initial version even worse, is completely detached from reality. For us and for the public, European Parliament documents and the European Parliament itself have unfortunately lost their value, as they do not serve the agenda of cooperation and dialogue," stated Levan Makhashvili, Chairman of the Parliamentary Committee on European Integration, responding to the report on Georgia adopted by the European Parliament's Foreign Affairs Committee.
According to him/her, the European Parliament's agenda today does not align with the Georgia-EU agenda or, more generally, with the agenda for Georgia's better and peaceful future.

"What can I tell you, you already know what we would do with this resolution [I would hand it in as waste paper] – for a simple reason: this document, along with its amendments which have made the initial version even worse, is completely detached from reality. It is especially clear during these days and weeks who is actually obstructing the dialogue. It is precisely the European Parliament, in the form of these specific political groups, who, driven by their own narrow political agendas, are doing their utmost to hinder dialogue. If we look at the developments of previous years, this is exactly what used to happen: whenever there was a prospect of resetting relations, dialogue, or cooperation, the European Parliament would swim completely against the tide, and we are witnessing the same thing today."

"Therefore, for us and for the public, both the European Parliament's documents and the European Parliament itself have, unfortunately, lost their value, as they do not serve the agenda of cooperation and dialogue. Today, the European Parliament's agenda is not in alignment with the Georgia-EU agenda, or with the agenda for Georgia's better, peaceful future in general," stated Levan Makhashvili.

When asked about the European Parliament's Foreign Affairs Committee calling for sanctions against several Georgian media outlets in its adopted report, Makhashvili replied that the statements and provisions in this specific document are "smile-inducing."

For information, the European Parliament's Committee on Foreign Affairs has adopted a report on Georgia. In the European Parliament's Committee on Foreign Affairs, 53 MEPs supported the annual report on Georgia, while 14 voted against it.
